what: A 2.2 µm cube with half of it cut away, leaving a block 1.1 µm thick, 1.1 × MIN_FEATURE, so it builds: micron-cube-halved's pair, at the bottom of the modelling range (kernel/CLAUDE.md).

recipe.do: Start a new part and delete its ready-made box (feature-1) from the timeline, as the L bracket's make does, so the counter goes on from 2.
Create Sketch on the top plane XY.
Rectangle tool, zoomed in: click (0, 0.0022), then (0.0022, 0.0044) (x 0..2.2 µm, y 2.2..4.4 µm; points 3, 4, 6, 8, lines 5, 7, 9, 10).
Extrude the sketch 0.0022 (z 0 to 2.2 µm): Body 1, the cube.
Create Sketch on the front plane XZ.

Rectangle tool: click (0.0011, −0.0022), then (0.0066, 0.0044) (x 1.1..6.6 µm, z −2.2..4.4 µm; points and lines 13 to 20). Seen along Y the cube's nearest offered point is its bottom edge's middle (0.0011, 0), 2.2 µm away, so nothing is pinned.
Extrude the sketch 0.0088, flipped (along +Y, y 0 to 8.8 µm): Body 2, the tool, through the cube from x = 1.1 µm on.
Combine: target Body 1, tool Body 2, Cut, Keep tools off.

volume.why: the cube's half x 0..1.1 µm: 1.1 × 2.2 × 2.2 µm

topology.why: a box: the tool's wall x = 1.1 µm closes the half; 8 − 12 + 6 = 2

box.why: the cube's from x = 0 to the tool's wall

tolerance.why: LINEAR (10 nm): every crossing here is between planes at round numbers, exact, so no intersection measures past LINEAR and nothing may grow (B0 decision 5: a crossing grows an entity only to what it measured)
